# Statements and keywords

Expressions evaluate to return a value.

Statements *do* something.

## Variable assignment statements

[Have seen variable assignment statements]

```{python}
# No output. This is a statement, it does not return a value.
x = 10
```

`x` is the variable *name*, `10` is the *value* of the variable `x`.

But the statement `x = 10` does not return a value.

```{python}
# Show the value of `x`.
x
```

https://realpython.com/ref/glossary/statement/

```{python}
# Expression (if expression is one number like this, it is also called a "literal").
2
```

```{python}
# Expression.
2 * 2
```

```{python}
# Statement (no value returned).
y = 2 * 2
```

## Assert statements

[Importance in software testing]

[Link this to data analysis also e.g. not just important for software devs!]

```{python tags=c("raises-exception")}
password = 10 + 2

assert type(password) == str
```

```{python tags=c("raises-exception")}
password = 10 + 2

assert type(password) == str, "Password is the wrong dtype!"
```

<!-- #region tags=["raises-exception"] -->
## Try, Except statements
<!-- #endregion -->

```{python}
result = stupid
```

```{python}
result = stupid
print('We will only see this print statement if the code runs this line...')
```

```{python}
try:
    result = stupid
except NameError:
    print("This made an error!")
print('We will only see this print statement if the code runs this line...')
```

## With statements

```{python}
url = "https://www.google.com/"

from urllib.request import urlopen

urlopen(url)
```

```{python}
type(urlopen(url))
```

[`with` automatically opens and closes a file]

```{python}
with urlopen(url) as webpage:
    # Read the content and decode it from bytes to text
    webpage_as_text = webpage.read().decode('utf-8')
print(webpage_as_text[:2000])
```

```{python}
from IPython.display import display, HTML

display(HTML(webpage_as_text))
```
